110: And from the place that you came  - this is not the teaching of the Tanna [i.e., this is no longer a quote from the baraita]; rather the Gemara proceeds to elaborate on the question that is being raised against Rav Yehudah, who had said earlier [Sotah 46a:11] that other types of loads disqualify the [red] heifer by mere placement. Since other types of loads are not [explicitly] written by the [red] heifer, and [must be] derived from the heifer [whose neck is broken] by way of verbal analogy -- you could have also derived from the place whence you came that just as a heifer [whose neck is broken is not qualified] until it pulls [the load], so too the [red] heifer [is not disqualified] by other types of loads until it pulls, since [its law] is derived from the heifer [whose neck is broken].
